newsitem.title: kazakhstan: Jail clash kills 20 prisoners in Tajikistan.
newsitem.headline: Jail clash kills 20 prisoners in Tajikistan.

text.p: About 20 inmates at a labour camp in northern Tajikistan were killed on Thursday when security forces stormed the camp to put down a riot, a senior regional official said on Friday.
"There were about 20 prisoners killed during the shooting," Olimdzhon Jalolov, a senior official with the northern Leninabad regional administration, told Reuters by telephone.
"After three days of fruitless negotiations with the riot leaders, the authorities were forced to send in police," Jalolov said.
He said about 30 prisoners and one policeman were also injured at the camp, in the regional capital of Khudjand.
"Today the situation is calm, we have imposed strict control," Jalolov said.
On Thursday officials at the former Soviet republic's Interior Ministry said order had already been restored at the camp and that three prison guards taken hostage had been released.
Tajikistan, a mountainous country bordering Afghanistan and China, is tentatively emerging from a bitter four-year civil war.
But Khudjand, separated from the rest of the country by mountains, has been largely untouched by the fighting.
Local residents contacted by telephone said shooting could be heard on the outskirts of town on Wednesday and Thursday and said armoured personnel carriers were deployed near the prison.
"One of the prison buildings was set on fire," said one resident. She said the police stormed the prison after fire engines sent in to put out the blaze were held by the prisoners.
An interior ministry source said elite OMON troops had been flown in from the capital Dushanbe to put down the riot, which began on Tuesday.
Jalolov said prisoners armed with iron bars had demanded the release of Ikrom Ashurov, the alleged leader of the riot, and 10 other inmates.
"Their demands were unacceptable for us, they were criminals, murderers," Jalolov said.
A militia source said Ashurov was killed in the clash.
Prison conditions in Central Asia are poor. Three prisoners were killed in a jail mutiny in a protest against overcrowding in Turkmenistan last year. Tuberculosis is widespread in Kazakh jails.
